resource.name: aws_autoscaling_group
resource.description: Provides an Auto Scaling Group resource. You must specify either launch_configuration, launch_template, or mixed_instances_policy. Terraform provides standalone Attachment (for attaching Classic Load Balancers and Application Load Balancer, Gateway Load Balancer, or Network Load Balancer target groups) and Traffic Source Attachment (for attaching Load Balancers and VPC Lattice target groups) resources and an Auto Scaling Group resource with load_balancers, target_group_arns and traffic_source attributes. Do not use the same traffic source in more than one of these resources. Doing so will cause a conflict of attachments. A lifecycle configuration block can be used to suppress differences if necessary. Hands-on: Try the Manage AWS Auto Scaling Groups tutorial on HashiCorp Learn.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_autoscaling_group` Terraform resource enables the creation and management of scalable, self-healing compute environments by automatically adjusting EC2 instance capacity based on demand. It is commonly used for configuring dynamic scaling policies, integrating with load balancers (Classic, Application, Gateway, or Network), and optimizing resource utilization in high-availability architectures. Users can define launch configurations, templates, or mixed instance policies, manage lifecycle settings, and attach traffic sources like target groups or VPC Lattice for seamless workload distribution and fault tolerance.

examples.title: With Latest Version Of Launch Template
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates how to configure an `aws_autoscaling_group` to use the latest version of an `aws_launch_template` for instance provisioning, showcasing the use of the `launch_template` block with the `version = "$Latest"` argument to ensure the most up-to-date template is applied."

examples.title: Mixed Instances Policy
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an `aws_autoscaling_group` with a mixed instances policy, enabling the use of multiple instance types and weighted capacities for flexible scaling. It showcases the `launch_template` block with overrides to specify alternative instance types (`c4.large`, `c3.large`) and their respective weighted capacities, providing a cost-effective and resilient scaling strategy.

examples.title: Mixed Instances Policy with Spot Instances and Capacity Rebalance
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates how to configure an `aws_autoscaling_group` with a mixed instances policy, utilizing Spot Instances with a `capacity-optimized` allocation strategy and enabling `capacity_rebalance` for improved availability. Includes overrides for instance types and weighted capacities, showcasing advanced scaling configurations for cost optimization and flexibility."

examples.title: Mixed Instances Policy with Instance level LaunchTemplateSpecification Overrides
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an `aws_autoscaling_group` with a mixed instances policy, utilizing multiple `aws_launch_template` resources and instance-level `launch_template_specification` overrides. It showcases how to define instance type overrides with custom weighted capacities and associate specific launch templates for advanced scaling flexibility across instance types.

examples.title: Mixed Instances Policy with Attribute-based Instance Type Selection
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an `aws_autoscaling_group` with a mixed instances policy that uses attribute-based instance type selection. It showcases the use of the `override` block within the `mixed_instances_policy` to define instance requirements, such as minimum memory and vCPU count, while leveraging a launch template for base configuration.

examples.title: Dynamic tagging
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to dynamically configure tags for an AWS Auto Scaling Group using the `dynamic` block in Terraform. It showcases the use of the `tag` argument to define both static and dynamically generated tags, with the `propagate_at_launch` attribute ensuring tags are applied to instances at launch.

examples.title: Automatically refresh all instances after the group is updated
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an `aws_autoscaling_group` with automatic instance refresh using the `instance_refresh` block, enabling rolling updates triggered by changes such as tags. It showcases integration with an `aws_launch_template` for instance configuration and highlights key settings like `min_healthy_percentage` for update preferences and `propagate_at_launch` for tag propagation.

examples.title: Auto Scaling group with Warm Pool
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates how to configure an AWS Auto Scaling Group with a Warm Pool to optimize instance readiness and scaling efficiency, using the `warm_pool` block with `pool_state` set to `Hibernated` and an `instance_reuse_policy` to enable instance reuse during scale-in events. Includes integration with an AWS Launch Template for specifying instance details like `image_id` and `instance_type`."

examples.title: Auto Scaling group with Traffic Sources
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates how to configure an AWS Auto Scaling Group with dynamic traffic sources using the `traffic_source` block, integrating with multiple VPC Lattice target groups. Highlights the use of `dynamic` blocks for flexible resource associations and the `force_delete` argument for seamless resource cleanup."

arguments.name: availability_zones
arguments.description: (Optional) A list of Availability Zones where instances in the Auto Scaling group can be created. Used for launching into the default VPC subnet in each Availability Zone when not using the `vpc_zone_identifier` attribute, or for attaching a network interface when an existing network interface ID is specified in a launch template. Conflicts with `vpc_zone_identifier`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `availability_zones` argument in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to specify the set of Availability Zones where instances in the Auto Scaling group can be launched. This configuration ensures high availability and fault tolerance by distributing instances across multiple zones, particularly when using the default VPC subnets or attaching existing network interfaces. It conflicts with `vpc_zone_identifier` and is typically used to define the geographic scope of the Auto Scaling group's infrastructure.

arguments.name: capacity_rebalance
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether capacity rebalance is enabled. Otherwise, capacity rebalance is disabled.
arguments.llm_summary: The `capacity_rebalance` argument in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to enable or disable the capacity rebalance feature, which automatically replaces instances in the Auto Scaling group that receive a Spot Instance interruption notice. Enabling this functionality helps maintain application availability and resilience by proactively reallocating capacity before interruptions occur, aligning with common goals of ensuring workload stability in dynamic cloud environments.

arguments.name: context
arguments.description: (Optional) Reserved.
arguments.llm_summary: The `context` argument in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource is a reserved field with no current functionality, meaning it does not directly influence the configuration or behavior of the Auto Scaling group. It may be intended for future use or internal purposes, and users typically do not need to set this argument.

arguments.name: default_cooldown
arguments.description: (Optional) Amount of time, in seconds, after a scaling activity completes before another scaling activity can start.
arguments.llm_summary: The `default_cooldown` argument for the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to define the cooldown period (in seconds) that must elapse after a scaling activity completes before another scaling action can be initiated. This helps control the frequency of scaling operations, ensuring stability and preventing excessive or rapid adjustments to the group's capacity.

arguments.name: default_instance_warmup
arguments.description: (Optional) Amount of time, in seconds, until a newly launched instance can contribute to the Amazon CloudWatch metrics. This delay lets an instance finish initializing before Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling aggregates instance metrics, resulting in more reliable usage data. Set this value equal to the amount of time that it takes for resource consumption to become stable after an instance reaches the InService state. (See Set the default instance warmup for an Auto Scaling group)
arguments.llm_summary: The `default_instance_warmup` argument for the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to define the initialization delay (in seconds) for newly launched instances before they contribute to Amazon CloudWatch metrics. This ensures more accurate and reliable metric aggregation by accounting for the time required for instances to stabilize after entering the `InService` state, supporting optimized scaling decisions and resource management.

arguments.name: desired_capacity
arguments.description: (Optional) Number of Amazon EC2 instances that should be running in the group. (See also Waiting for Capacity below.)
arguments.llm_summary: The `desired_capacity` argument in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource specifies the target number of Amazon EC2 instances that should be running in the Auto Scaling group at any given time. By setting this value, users can control the baseline capacity of the group to meet application demands, ensuring consistent performance and resource availability while balancing cost efficiency.

arguments.name: desired_capacity_type
arguments.description: (Optional) The unit of measurement for the value specified for `desired_capacity`. Supported for attribute-based instance type selection only. Valid values: `"units"`, `"vcpu"`, `"memory-mib"`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `desired_capacity_type` argument in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to specify the unit of measurement for the `desired_capacity` value, enabling precise control over how the scaling group determines resource allocation. By setting this argument to `"units"`, `"vcpu"`, or `"memory-mib"`, users can align scaling behavior with attribute-based instance type selection, optimizing resource provisioning to meet specific workload requirements such as compute power or memory capacity.

arguments.name: enabled_metrics
arguments.description: (Optional) List of metrics to collect. The allowed values are defined by the underlying AWS API.
arguments.llm_summary: The `enabled_metrics` argument for the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to specify a set of metrics to be collected for the Auto Scaling group, enabling detailed monitoring of its performance and operational health. By defining this argument, users can configure which metrics (e.g., group size, instance lifecycle events) are reported to CloudWatch, supporting goals like optimizing scaling policies, troubleshooting, and ensuring resource efficiency.

arguments.name: force_delete
arguments.description: (Optional) Allows deleting the Auto Scaling Group without waiting for all instances in the pool to terminate. You can force an Auto Scaling Group to delete even if it's in the process of scaling a resource. Normally, Terraform drains all the instances before deleting the group. This bypasses that behavior and potentially leaves resources dangling.
arguments.llm_summary: The `force_delete` argument in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to control the deletion behavior of the Auto Scaling Group by bypassing the default instance draining process. When set to `true`, it enables immediate deletion of the group, even if instances are still running or scaling activities are in progress, which can expedite teardown workflows but may leave associated resources unmanaged.

arguments.name: force_delete_warm_pool
arguments.description: (Optional) Allows deleting the Auto Scaling Group without waiting for all instances in the warm pool to terminate.
arguments.llm_summary: The `force_delete_warm_pool` argument in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to control the deletion behavior of the Auto Scaling Group by enabling the immediate removal of the associated warm pool without waiting for its instances to terminate. This is useful for streamlining lifecycle management during resource cleanup or decommissioning, especially in scenarios where instance termination delays are not critical.

arguments.name: health_check_grace_period
arguments.description: (Optional, Default: 300) Time (in seconds) after instance comes into service before checking health.
arguments.llm_summary: The `health_check_grace_period` argument for the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource defines the time (in seconds) to wait after a new instance is launched and marked as "in service" before performing health checks. This allows users to account for initialization processes, ensuring instances are not prematurely marked unhealthy during startup, which is critical for maintaining application stability and avoiding unnecessary replacements.

arguments.name: health_check_type
arguments.description: (Optional) "EC2" or "ELB". Controls how health checking is done.
arguments.llm_summary: The `health_check_type` argument in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to specify the method used to evaluate the health of instances within the Auto Scaling group, either through EC2 instance status checks (`"EC2"`) or Elastic Load Balancer (ELB) health checks (`"ELB"`). Configuring this argument ensures the Auto Scaling group uses the appropriate health monitoring mechanism to determine whether instances should be replaced or terminated, aligning with the user's infrastructure and load balancing strategy.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument for the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to specify a unique identifier for the autoscaling group, typically used for referencing or managing the resource programmatically. While optional, setting this argument can help ensure consistent identification of the autoscaling group across Terraform configurations and integrations, supporting workflows that require explicit resource tracking or external system interactions.

arguments.name: ignore_failed_scaling_activities
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether to ignore failed Auto Scaling scaling activities while waiting for capacity. The default is `false` -- failed scaling activities cause errors to be returned.
arguments.llm_summary: The `ignore_failed_scaling_activities` argument in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to control whether failed scaling activities are ignored during capacity adjustments. Setting this to `true` ensures the Auto Scaling process continues without errors caused by failed scaling attempts, which can be useful for maintaining availability in dynamic environments or during transient issues.

arguments.name: launch_configuration
arguments.description: (Optional) Name of the launch configuration to use.
arguments.llm_summary: The `launch_configuration` argument in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to specify the name of an existing launch configuration that defines the instance settings (e.g., AMI, instance type, key pair, security groups) for the Auto Scaling group. By setting this argument, users can control the provisioning behavior and runtime configuration of EC2 instances launched within the group, aligning with deployment requirements and scaling strategies.

arguments.name: load_balancers
arguments.description: (Optional) List of elastic load balancer names to add to the autoscaling group names. Only valid for classic load balancers. For ALBs, use `target_group_arns` instead. To remove all load balancer attachments an empty list should be specified.
arguments.llm_summary: The `load_balancers` argument in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to associate a list of classic Elastic Load Balancer (ELB) names with the Auto Scaling group, enabling automatic distribution of incoming traffic across instances in the group. This configuration is essential for users managing legacy load balancing setups, as it ensures seamless traffic routing and scaling, but should be replaced with `target_group_arns` for modern Application Load Balancers (ALBs).

arguments.name: max_instance_lifetime
arguments.description: (Optional) Maximum amount of time, in seconds, that an instance can be in service, values must be either equal to 0 or between 86400 and 31536000 seconds.
arguments.llm_summary: The `max_instance_lifetime` argument in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to define the maximum duration, in seconds, that an EC2 instance can remain in service before being replaced. This configuration helps enforce instance lifecycle policies, ensuring instances are periodically refreshed to maintain performance, security, or compliance standards.

arguments.name: max_size
arguments.description: (Required) Maximum size of the Auto Scaling Group.
arguments.llm_summary: The `max_size` argument defines the maximum number of instances that the Auto Scaling Group can scale up to, allowing users to control the upper limit of compute resources for handling peak workloads. This ensures the group does not exceed a specified capacity, aligning with cost management and performance requirements.

arguments.name: metrics_granularity
arguments.description: (Optional) Granularity to associate with the metrics to collect. The only valid value is `1Minute`. Default is `1Minute`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `metrics_granularity` argument in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource specifies the level of detail for monitoring metrics collected from the Auto Scaling group, with the only valid option being `1Minute`. By configuring this argument, users enable high-resolution metric collection at one-minute intervals, supporting detailed performance analysis and fine-grained scaling decisions.

arguments.name: min_elb_capacity
arguments.description: (Optional) Setting this causes Terraform to wait for this number of instances from this Auto Scaling Group to show up healthy in the ELB only on creation. Updates will not wait on ELB instance number changes. (See also Waiting for Capacity below.)
arguments.llm_summary: The `min_elb_capacity` argument for the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to define the minimum number of instances that must be registered as healthy in the associated Elastic Load Balancer (ELB) during the initial creation of the Auto Scaling Group. This ensures that a baseline capacity is met for load balancing before Terraform considers the resource creation complete, supporting user goals related to application availability and reliability during deployment.

arguments.name: min_size
arguments.description: (Required) Minimum size of the Auto Scaling Group. (See also Waiting for Capacity below.)
arguments.llm_summary: The `min_size` argument for the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource specifies the minimum number of instances that must always be running in the Auto Scaling Group, ensuring baseline capacity to meet application demands or maintain system availability. By defining this value, users can control the group's lower bound for scaling, aligning with reliability and performance goals in dynamic environments.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Optional) Name of the Auto Scaling Group. By default generated by Terraform. Conflicts with `name_prefix`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name` argument for the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to explicitly define a unique, human-readable identifier for the Auto Scaling Group, overriding Terraform's default name generation. This is useful for aligning the resource with naming conventions, improving clarity in resource management, and ensuring predictable integration with other systems or workflows. Note that it conflicts with the `name_prefix` argument.

arguments.name: name_prefix
arguments.description: (Optional) Creates a unique name beginning with the specified prefix. Conflicts with `name`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name_prefix` argument for the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to define a unique, automatically generated name for the Auto Scaling group that begins with the specified prefix. This is useful for dynamically creating resource names in environments where naming conventions or uniqueness are required, such as managing multiple environments or automating deployments. It cannot be used alongside the `name` argument.

arguments.name: placement_group
arguments.description: (Optional) Name of the placement group into which you'll launch your instances, if any.
arguments.llm_summary: The `placement_group` argument in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to specify the name of an existing placement group where instances in the Auto Scaling group will be launched. This enables users to optimize instance placement for specific workloads, such as achieving low-latency networking or high-performance computing, aligning with goals like improving resource efficiency or meeting specialized infrastructure requirements.

arguments.name: protect_from_scale_in
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether newly launched instances are automatically protected from termination by Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling when scaling in. For more information about preventing instances from terminating on scale in, see Using instance scale-in protection in the Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling User Guide.
arguments.llm_summary: The `protect_from_scale_in` argument in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to define whether newly launched instances are automatically safeguarded from termination during scale-in operations. This configuration is typically used to ensure critical instances remain active, supporting lifecycle management and high availability goals within an Auto Scaling group.

arguments.name: service_linked_role_arn
arguments.description: (Optional) ARN of the service-linked role that the ASG will use to call other AWS services
arguments.llm_summary: The `service_linked_role_arn` argument allows users to specify the ARN of a service-linked IAM role that the Auto Scaling Group (ASG) will use to interact with other AWS services on their behalf. Configuring this ensures the ASG has the necessary permissions to perform tasks like scaling instances or managing resources, aligning with specific security and operational requirements.

arguments.name: suspended_processes
arguments.description: (Optional) List of processes to suspend for the Auto Scaling Group. The allowed values are `Launch`, `Terminate`, `HealthCheck`, `ReplaceUnhealthy`, `AZRebalance`, `AlarmNotification`, `ScheduledActions`, `AddToLoadBalancer`, `InstanceRefresh`. Note that if you suspend either the `Launch` or `Terminate` process types, it can prevent your Auto Scaling Group from functioning properly.
arguments.llm_summary: The `suspended_processes` argument for the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to specify which scaling-related processes (e.g., `Launch`, `Terminate`, `HealthCheck`) should be temporarily disabled for the Auto Scaling Group. This configuration is typically used to control or pause specific operational behaviors, such as instance launches or health checks, to support maintenance, debugging, or custom workflows, but suspending critical processes like `Launch` or `Terminate` may impact the group's functionality.

arguments.name: target_group_arns
arguments.description: (Optional) Set of `aws_alb_target_group` ARNs, for use with Application or Network Load Balancing. To remove all target group attachments an empty list should be specified.
arguments.llm_summary: The `target_group_arns` argument allows users to associate an Auto Scaling group with one or more Application or Network Load Balancer target groups by specifying their ARNs. This configuration enables the Auto Scaling group to dynamically register or deregister instances with the specified target groups, facilitating load balancing and traffic distribution for scalable applications.

arguments.name: termination_policies
arguments.description: (Optional) List of policies to decide how the instances in the Auto Scaling Group should be terminated. The allowed values are `OldestInstance`, `NewestInstance`, `OldestLaunchConfiguration`, `ClosestToNextInstanceHour`, `OldestLaunchTemplate`, `AllocationStrategy`, `Default`. Additionally, the ARN of a Lambda function can be specified for custom termination policies.
arguments.llm_summary: The `termination_policies` argument in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to define the rules and priorities for determining which instances should be terminated during scaling or group updates. By specifying policies such as `OldestInstance`, `NewestInstance`, or custom Lambda function ARNs, users can control the lifecycle behavior of instances to align with operational goals like cost optimization, instance freshness, or custom termination logic.

arguments.name: vpc_zone_identifier
arguments.description: (Optional) List of subnet IDs to launch resources in. Subnets automatically determine which availability zones the group will reside. Conflicts with `availability_zones`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `vpc_zone_identifier` argument for the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to specify a set of subnet IDs within a VPC where the Auto Scaling group will launch its instances. By defining this argument, users control the placement of resources across specific subnets, which inherently determines the availability zones used by the group. This configuration is essential for aligning instance deployment with network architecture and ensuring high availability or compliance with specific subnet-level requirements.

arguments.name: wait_for_capacity_timeout
arguments.description: (Optional, Default: "10m") Maximum duration that Terraform should wait for ASG instances to be healthy before timing out. (See also Waiting for Capacity below.) Setting this to "0" causes Terraform to skip all Capacity Waiting behavior.
arguments.llm_summary: The `wait_for_capacity_timeout` argument in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to define the maximum duration Terraform will wait for Auto Scaling Group instances to reach a healthy state during deployment. By configuring this timeout, users can control the behavior of capacity waiting, ensuring deployments either proceed after the specified time or skip health checks entirely when set to "0," aligning with goals like optimizing deployment speed or enforcing stricter health validation.

arguments.name: wait_for_elb_capacity
arguments.description: (Optional) Setting this will cause Terraform to wait for exactly this number of healthy instances from this Auto Scaling Group in all attached load balancers on both create and update operations. (Takes precedence over `min_elb_capacity` behavior.) (See also Waiting for Capacity below.)
arguments.llm_summary: The `wait_for_elb_capacity` argument in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to specify the exact number of healthy instances that must be registered with all attached load balancers before Terraform considers the Auto Scaling Group creation or update complete. This ensures precise control over deployment readiness and load balancer health checks, supporting user goals like reliable application scaling and minimizing downtime during infrastructure changes.

blocks.name: availability_zone_distribution
blocks.description: (Optional) The instance capacity distribution across Availability Zones. See Availability Zone Distribution below for more details.

arguments.name: capacity_distribution_strategy
arguments.description: (Required) The strategy to use for distributing capacity across the Availability Zones. Valid values are `balanced-only` and `balanced-best-effort`. Default is `balanced-best-effort`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `capacity_distribution_strategy` argument in the `availability_zone_distribution` context of the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to define how instance capacity is distributed across Availability Zones within the Auto Scaling Group. By specifying either `balanced-only` or `balanced-best-effort`, users can control whether capacity is strictly balanced or optimized for best effort in scenarios with uneven resource availability, ensuring efficient scaling and high availability across zones.

blocks.llm_summary: The `availability_zone_distribution` block in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource configures how instance capacity is distributed across multiple Availability Zones, ensuring balanced resource allocation and high availability. By defining this block, users can optimize fault tolerance and scalability within their Auto Scaling Groups, enabling precise control over zone-level capacity management.

blocks.name: initial_lifecycle_hook
blocks.description: (Optional) One or more Lifecycle Hooks to attach to the Auto Scaling Group before instances are launched. The syntax is exactly the same as the separate `aws_autoscaling_lifecycle_hook` resource, without the `autoscaling_group_name` attribute. Please note that this will only work when creating a new Auto Scaling Group. For all other use-cases, please use `aws_autoscaling_lifecycle_hook` resource.

arguments.name: default_result
arguments.llm_summary: The `default_result` argument in the `initial_lifecycle_hook` of the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to specify the default action taken when a lifecycle hook times out without receiving a callback. This argument controls whether the instance proceeds (`CONTINUE`) or is terminated (`ABANDON`), enabling users to define the fallback behavior for managing instance transitions during scaling events.

arguments.name: heartbeat_timeout
arguments.llm_summary: The `heartbeat_timeout` argument for the `initial_lifecycle_hook` in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource specifies the maximum time (in seconds) that an instance can remain in the "Pending:Wait" or "Terminating:Wait" state while the lifecycle hook is active. By configuring this timeout, users can control how long an external process or system has to complete tasks (e.g., initialization, cleanup, or custom workflows) before the instance transitions to the next lifecycle state, ensuring smoother automation and integration with external systems.

arguments.name: lifecycle_transition
arguments.llm_summary: The `lifecycle_transition` argument specifies the lifecycle event in the Auto Scaling process (e.g., `autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHING` or `autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATING`) that triggers the associated `initial_lifecycle_hook`. By defining this transition, users can control when custom actions or processes are executed during instance launch or termination, enabling fine-grained management of application state or resource cleanup.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Optional) Name of the Auto Scaling Group. By default generated by Terraform. Conflicts with `name_prefix`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name` argument for the `initial_lifecycle_hook` in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to explicitly define a unique identifier for the lifecycle hook, ensuring precise control over its configuration and behavior within the Auto Scaling Group. By setting this argument, users can establish a clear reference for managing lifecycle transitions, such as custom actions during instance launch or termination, aligning with specific operational workflows or automation requirements.

arguments.name: notification_metadata
arguments.llm_summary: The `notification_metadata` argument for the `initial_lifecycle_hook` in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to specify a custom string of metadata that is sent alongside lifecycle hook notifications. This enables users to include contextual information, such as environment details or operational instructions, which can be leveraged by downstream systems or processes to handle the lifecycle event more effectively.

arguments.name: notification_target_arn
arguments.llm_summary: The `notification_target_arn` argument for the `initial_lifecycle_hook` in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource specifies the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the target (e.g., an SNS topic or SQS queue) to which lifecycle hook notifications are sent. Configuring this argument enables users to define where notifications about instance launch or termination transitions are delivered, facilitating automated workflows or monitoring during the Auto Scaling process.

arguments.name: role_arn
arguments.llm_summary: The `role_arn` argument specifies the ARN of an IAM role that grants permissions for the initial lifecycle hook to perform actions, such as invoking AWS services or sending notifications during Auto Scaling events. Configuring this argument allows users to define the role responsible for managing lifecycle transitions, enabling custom workflows or integrations during instance launch or termination.

blocks.llm_summary: The `initial_lifecycle_hook` block in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to define one or more lifecycle hooks that execute custom actions during specific instance state transitions (e.g., before launch or termination) within the Auto Scaling Group. This configuration encapsulates lifecycle management settings, enabling users to integrate workflows such as logging, monitoring, or configuration scripts during instance initialization or shutdown, ensuring greater control and automation in scaling operations.

blocks.name: instance_maintenance_policy
blocks.description: (Optional) If this block is configured, add a instance maintenance policy to the specified Auto Scaling group. Defined below.

arguments.name: max_healthy_percentage
arguments.description: (Required) Specifies the upper limit on the number of instances that are in the InService or Pending state with a healthy status during an instance replacement activity.
arguments.llm_summary: The `max_healthy_percentage` argument in the `instance_maintenance_policy` of the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource defines the maximum percentage of instances allowed to remain in a healthy state (InService or Pending) during instance replacement activities. This ensures controlled instance turnover while maintaining high availability, enabling users to balance system stability and maintenance efficiency.

arguments.name: min_healthy_percentage
arguments.description: (Required) Specifies the lower limit on the number of instances that must be in the InService state with a healthy status during an instance replacement activity.
arguments.llm_summary: The `min_healthy_percentage` argument in the `instance_maintenance_policy` of the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource defines the minimum percentage of instances that must remain in the `InService` state and marked as healthy during instance replacement activities. This ensures high availability and continuity by controlling the threshold for healthy instances, aligning with user goals of maintaining application stability during scaling or maintenance operations.

blocks.llm_summary: The `instance_maintenance_policy` block in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource defines policies for managing the maintenance and lifecycle of instances within the Auto Scaling group. It encapsulates settings that enable users to control how instances are handled during maintenance events, ensuring operational stability and alignment with scaling strategies. Configuring this block allows users to optimize instance behavior during updates or maintenance, enhancing reliability and minimizing disruptions.

blocks.name: instance_refresh
blocks.description: (Optional) If this block is configured, start an Instance Refresh when this Auto Scaling Group is updated. Defined below.

arguments.name: strategy
arguments.description: (Required) Strategy to use for instance refresh. The only allowed value is `Rolling`. See StartInstanceRefresh Action for more information.
arguments.llm_summary: The `strategy` argument in the `instance_refresh` configuration of the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource specifies the method used to update instances within the Auto Scaling group during a refresh operation. By setting this required argument to `Rolling`, users define a rolling update strategy, ensuring instances are replaced incrementally to maintain application availability and minimize downtime during updates.

arguments.name: triggers
arguments.description: (Optional) Set of additional property names that will trigger an Instance Refresh. A refresh will always be triggered by a change in any of `launch_configuration`, `launch_template`, or `mixed_instances_policy`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `triggers` argument in the `instance_refresh` block of the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to specify additional property names that will initiate an Instance Refresh when their values change. arguments.name: alarms
arguments.description: (Required) List of Cloudwatch alarms. If any of these alarms goes into ALARM state, Instance Refresh is failed. A refresh is started when any of the following Auto Scaling Group properties change: launch_configuration, launch_template, mixed_instances_policy. Additional properties can be specified in the triggers property of instance_refresh. A refresh will not start when version = "$Latest" is configured in the launch_template block. To trigger the instance refresh when a launch template is changed, configure version to use the latest_version attribute of the aws_launch_template resource. Auto Scaling Groups support up to one active instance refresh at a time. When this resource is updated, any existing refresh is cancelled. Depending on health check settings and group size, an instance refresh may take a long time or fail. This resource does not wait for the instance refresh to complete.
arguments.llm_summary: The `alarms` argument in the `alarm_specification` block of the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource allows users to specify a list of CloudWatch alarm names that act as failure conditions for an instance refresh operation. If any of the defined alarms enter the `ALARM` state during the refresh, the operation is terminated, ensuring tighter control over the health and stability of the Auto Scaling Group during updates triggered by changes to configurations like launch templates or policies.

blocks.llm_summary: The `alarm_specification` block within the `preferences` context of the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource defines monitoring criteria for instance refresh operations by specifying a list of required CloudWatch alarms. Configuring this block enables users to enforce automated failure detection during instance refreshes, ensuring operational stability by halting the process if any specified alarm enters an ALARM state.

The `preferences` configuration block within the `instance_refresh` context of the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource provides granular control over the behavior and parameters of instance refresh operations. It encapsulates settings for checkpoint timing, instance warmup, health capacity thresholds, alarm handling, and behaviors for protected or standby instances, enabling users to customize the refresh process to ensure minimal disruption, optimize resource availability, and automate rollback in case of failures. Configuring this block allows users to fine-tune the refresh lifecycle to align with workload requirements and operational constraints.

The `instance_refresh` block in the `aws_autoscaling_group` resource enables automated updates to instances within the Auto Scaling Group by initiating an Instance Refresh during configuration changes. It encapsulates settings related to instance replacement and update strategies, allowing users to ensure seamless, controlled updates to maintain application availability and consistency during scaling or infrastructure modifications.
